articles.title: Meta is closing down three VR studios as part of its metaverse cuts
articles.summary: Meta’s Reality Labs layoffs include shutting down some of its VR studios, according to employees affected by the cuts.
articles.body: Meta is laying off about 10 percent of its Reality Labs metaverse division, and the cuts include closing down some of its VR gaming studios. Twisted Pixel Games, the developer of Marvel’s Deadpool VR, Sanzaru Games, the developer of the Asgard’s Wrath franchise, and Armature Studio, which worked on the Resident Evil 4 VR port, are all being closed down, according to an internal memo viewed by Bloomberg. The team behind the VR fitness app Supernatural will no longer develop new content or features for it, though the “existing product” will still be supported, Bloomberg says. Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton confirmed to The Verge that Bloomberg’s reporting is accurate. Laid off staffers have posted about the closures online. * “I’ve just been laid off. It appears the entire Twisted Pixel Games studio has been shut down along with Sanzaru and Armature too,” former Twisted Pixel level designer Andy Gentile says. * “Unfortunately, Twisted Pixel Games has been closed as a result of strategy changes at Meta,” former Twisted Pixel senior artist Dan Greenfield says. * “As many will hear soon, several Meta game studios were closed today, including Sanzaru,” former Sanzaru senior level designer Ray West says. * “Due to an unexpected closure of Sanzaru Studios, I’m open for work,” former Sanzaru lead environment artist Tyler Fluharty says. Meta acquired Supernatural developer Within in 2023 (after a fight with the FTC), Twisted Pixel and Armature in 2022, and Sanzaru in 2020. The company closed Echo VR developer Ready at Dawn, which it also acquired in 2020, in 2024. In a statement about the broader Reality Labs layoffs, Clayton said that “We said last month that we were shifting some of our investment from Metaverse toward Wearables. This is part of that effort, and we plan to reinvest the savings to support the growth of wearables this year.” Update, January 13th: Added details from Bloomberg about the studio closures.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Marilyn Monroe: ‘I don't understand why people aren't a little more generous with each other’ — the Hollywood icon's powerful lesson on kindness and empathy
articles.summary: Explore Marilyn Monroe's poignant reflection on empathy and kindness, highlighting the impact of our words. Discover how her experiences shaped her simple yet profound lesson on treating others with generosity, relevant even in today's digital world.
articles.body: It's funny how something as small as a passing comment can stay with someone for years. Maybe someone made an unnecessary remark about your appearance, judged a decision you made or was simply rude for no particular reason. They might not even remember saying it, but you probably do.Marilyn Monroe knew what it was like to have people constantly talking about her. Being one of Hollywood's biggest stars meant that almost everything she did attracted attention, and not all of it was kind. During one of her final interviews, she spoke about this and made a rather simple observation about how people treat one another.Today's quote of the day by Marilyn Monroe reads: “I don't understand why people aren't a little more generous with each other.”She shared these words during conversations with LIFE associate editor Richard Meryman in July 1962. The interview, titled 'Last Talk With a Lonely Girl: Marilyn Monroe', appeared in LIFE magazine on August 17, 1962. A shortened version was later published by The Guardian on September 14, 2007, as part of its Great Interviews of the 20th Century series.Monroe spoke about the less glamorous side of fame, including the insults, jealousy and judgement she had experienced. So, her comment about being more generous wasn't just a random thought about kindness. It came from someone who had spent years dealing with other people's opinions of her.What does the quote by Marilyn Monroe mean?Marilyn Monroe's words are quite straightforward, but there's a reason they stay with you. She's talking about the little things we often don't think twice about.We've all had moments when someone was unnecessarily harsh, or when we said something in irritation and realised later that we could have handled it differently. It doesn't always take a big argument to upset someone. Sometimes, it's just one careless remark.Being generous with people doesn't mean agreeing with everything they say or letting them get away with bad behaviour. It can be as simple as not assuming the worst about someone, listening before judging or knowing when a comment doesn't need to be made.And honestly, these things aren't always easy. We all have bad days, get impatient and occasionally take our frustration out on the wrong person. But that doesn't mean we can't make a little more effort.How is the quote by Marilyn Monroe relevant today?Marilyn Monroe made this observation decades before social media became part of everyday life, but it feels particularly familiar now.Think about how quickly people form opinions online. Someone shares a photograph, talks about their relationship or makes a personal choice, and suddenly complete strangers have something to say about it. Sometimes the comments are far from kind, and the fact that they're posted behind a screen seems to make people less careful about their words.Monroe experienced a version of this throughout her career. Millions admired her, but she was also constantly photographed, discussed and judged. Being famous didn't mean she was spared the unpleasant side of human behaviour.That's perhaps what makes her words worth revisiting. Being admired doesn't make someone immune to hurt, and being a stranger doesn't mean we should treat someone without consideration.Early life of Marilyn MonroeBefore the world knew her as Marilyn Monroe, she was Norma Jeane Mortenson, born on June 1, 1926, in Los Angeles, California. Her childhood was far removed from the glamorous image people would eventually associate with her. She spent much of her early life in foster homes and dealt with an unstable family environment.Her interest in films grew as she got older, and modelling eventually gave her a way into the entertainment industry. Those early opportunities would go on to change the course of her life.How did Marilyn Monroe rise to fame?Marilyn Monroe didn't become a Hollywood star overnight. She started with smaller roles before getting noticed in films such as 'Niagara', 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes' and 'The Seven Year Itch', all released in 1953.She was often associated with her glamorous image, but Monroe wanted audiences to take her acting seriously, too. Films such as 'Bus Stop' and 'Some Like It Hot' gave her the opportunity to show a different side of herself. Her performance in the latter earned her a Golden Globe in 1960.Even today, people recognise her face and name almost instantly. But interviews like the one she gave Richard Meryman offer something beyond the familiar Hollywood image. They give us a glimpse of what she thought about life and the people around her. And sometimes, it's these smaller observations that stay with us longer than the glamorous photographs.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Australian Influencer’s Bali Vacation Ends in ICU After Headache Turns Out to Be Meningitis
articles.summary: Australian fitness influencer woke up with a bad headache in Bali but has spent over a week in a hospital intensive care unit due to meningitis. Meningitis i...
articles.body:
Australian fitness influencer woke up with a bad headache in Bali but has spent over a week in a hospital intensive care unit due to meningitis. Meningitis is an infection of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord and can be fatal if not treated quickly.

Khiana Smith, 23, a fitness creator and online coach from Gold Coast, Australia, told news.com.au that she had been in intensive care for eight days with bacterial and viral meningitis, pneumonia she got in the hospital, and fluid in her lungs, according to the New York Post .

"I just woke up one day, and I had the worst headache," Smith said.

Smith runs Her Method, a fitness and nutrition coaching business, and has been posting updates from her hospital bed to TikTok and Instagram, where she has nearly 87,000 followers combined, TMZ reported.

Smith had been traveling in Europe for two weeks and had been in Bali for about a week when she fell ill, the Post reported. The headache quickly turned into severe head pain, dizziness, slurred speech, blurred vision, and extreme sensitivity to light, UNILAD reported , citing her posts.

IV drip treatment she had at the villa did not improve her symptoms, and a doctor who checked her called an ambulance, which took her to a hospital within minutes. Within a few hours, she had a CT scan and intravenous antibiotics, a quick response that her mother said probably saved her life.

Doctors do not yet know how she was infected. Possible sources include contaminated food, water she swam in, or another passenger on a flight.

Her stories have slight discrepancies. Smith told news.com.au she had been in intensive care for eight days, while TMZ said nine. The infection has left her with memory problems and difficulties following conversations.

"I really struggle to remember things," Smith said in a TikTok video.

She also had to deal with language barriers as she tried to understand her condition, UNILAD reported. In her latest update, Smith said she felt a bit better after getting out of bed and walking for the first time in more than a week.

Her mother, Cass Smith, flew to Indonesia as soon as she found out her daughter was ill. She told news.com.au that nothing is scarier than knowing her child is struggling for her life in another country, thousands of kilometers from home, the Post reported.

The family commended Indonesian medical staff despite the language barrier. When her condition deteriorated, doctors were able to reach Smith within 10 to 15 minutes, a level of care the family said is more than they usually get in Australian hospitals.

Travel insurance is covering her hospital bills. Cass Smith said she warned her daughter to buy a policy before the trip and advised other travelers to do the same.

Smith has not been cleared to fly back home due to swelling in her brain and concerns about cabin pressure. The family hopes doctors will give her clearance in about a week, when she plans to cut her trip short and recover on the Gold Coast. They also hope the quick start of antibiotics will prevent any long-term consequences and that her memory loss will be temporary.

Hundreds of followers have sent her messages of support. Smith, who says she eats healthy and exercises every day, has used her posts to warn others that serious illness can happen to anyone.

"Don't take your life or health for granted ever," she told her followers, according to UNILAD.

Meningitis is swelling of the protective lining of the brain and spinal cord. Bacterial meningitis is a serious illness and can kill in a few hours, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says. Most people recover with proper care, but survivors may suffer permanent disabilities, and complications can include seizures, coma, and even death. Doctors treat it with antibiotics, which the CDC says should start as soon as possible.

Viral meningitis is the most common type and is less serious. Most people recover from mild cases on their own within seven to 10 days, though severe cases may require hospitalization, the CDC says.

Bali has a reputation for having bacterial meningitis. A 2019 study in Emerging Infectious Diseases , a CDC journal, found that 44 of 71 cases of acute bacterial meningitis treated at Denpasar's main hospital from 2014 to 2017 were caused by Streptococcus suis, a bacterium carried by pigs. Researchers attributed those infections primarily to handling pigs and eating raw pork products, including traditional dishes made from fresh pig blood. About 11% of the patients in the study died.

No particular cause has been announced in Smith's case.

Its domestic performance also showed a slight improvement compared to the previous day. Meanwhile, the film's overseas business continued to contribute significantly to its overall earnings.'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' Day 31 box office collectionAccording to Sacnilk, 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' collected Rs 1.75 crore in India net earnings on Sunday, November 1. Sunday contributed the highest share, with the thriller registering a better collection than the previous day.The film's overseas performance also added to its impressive worldwide total. With its domestic and international earnings combined, the Ajay Devgn starrer has reached a worldwide gross collection of Rs 584.74 crore.'Drishyam 3' week-wise performanceIts opening week remains the biggest contributor to its domestic earnings. articles.title: Andrew Shue marries Marilee Fiebig, weeks after their exes Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes tied the knot
articles.summary: The couple’s “low-key” ceremony was held at their 92-acre New Jersey estate on Sunday.
articles.body:
Andrew Shue and Marilee Fiebig have tied the knot after three years of dating.

The Melrose Place star and immigration attorney wed in a "low-key" ceremony at their 92-acre New Jersey estate on Sunday.

Shue and Fiebig bonded after their respective former spouses, Good Morning America anchors Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes, went public with their relationship in 2022.

Andrew Shue and Marilee Fiebig are officially married!

The Melrose Place alum and the immigration attorney tied the knot on Sunday in a "low-key" ceremony at their 92-acre estate outside of Stockton, N.J., confirms Entertainment Weekly 's sister site PEOPLE . The Daily Mail also published photos of Fiebig in her white lace wedding gown.

The nuptials come just days after news broke that Shue and Fiebig were engaged . The couple famously bonded after their former spouses, Good Morning America anchors Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes, were romantically linked .

Robach and Holmes, meanwhile, got married last month in Arkansas.

"We're very grateful and hopeful," Shue told PEOPLE last week about his engagement to Fiebig. "I don't know how it happened, but there's a happy ending."

The photographs of the wedding show Sabine, Fiebig's 13-year-old daughter with Holmes, serving as one of her bridesmaids alongside the attorney's close friend, finance executive Lisa Bashishow. The groom's sister, Oscar-nominated Leaving Las Vegas actress Elisabeth Shue, also attended the ceremony.

Entertainment Weekly has reached out to representatives for Shue and Fiebig for comment.

Shue and Fiebig, coincidentally, were both married to their previous spouses from 2010 to 2023. Fiebig and Holmes share Sabine, while Shue did not have any children with Robach.

"Relationships are hard. They're messy. They're not perfect. We have fought for love, and I can say I have never been happier. I am with my best friend," Robach said in December 2023, a year after her relationship with Holmes came to light, resulting in the couple's exit from GMA .

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

"Marilee's sole focus has remained on the overall best interest of her 9-year-old daughter," an attorney for Fiebig said at the time .

For his part, Shue reflected on how the end of his marriage to Robach led to him finding "The One."

"I had to accept my own part in marriage not working out for me and in not understanding myself well enough and not understanding what matters in a relationship well enough to find the right person for me, and that has been an extraordinary gift," he told PEOPLE . articles.title: How one Shrewsbury musician turned disability and isolation into a song
articles.summary: Nikki Rous says music has become a way of processing the challenges of disability and illness.
articles.body:
When people talk about disability, the conversation often focuses on symptoms, treatment and physical barriers.

Less often discussed is the loneliness that can accompany chronic illness and disability.

For singer-songwriter Nikki Rous, a wheelchair user, that experience became the inspiration for a new song exploring the isolation that can accompany disability and chronic illness.

"I think as a disabled person, and [with] many other people that suffer from chronic illness, chronic pain and disability, there's a certain amount of isolation," she said.

"It's a very different lifestyle to when I was able-bodied.

"I just wanted to get that point across really about the loneliness and isolation and hopefully make some people feel not so alone."

Her latest song, No Space Left, draws on personal experience, but touches on feelings that many people living with long-term health conditions may recognise.

For Rous, songwriting has become a way of processing experiences that can be difficult to explain.

"It's quite cathartic for me," she said.

"If I'm having a tough time, I'll generally write it all out, produce a song and then I've kind of moved on from that place."

The song is informed in part by her experience of living with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) , a group of rare inherited conditions that affect the body's connective tissues.

Connective tissue supports the skin, joints, blood vessels and organs, and symptoms can include chronic pain, fatigue and mobility problems.

Rous said EDS was the condition she was born with, although she also lives with other related conditions.

"It's a genetic connective tissue disorder that affects your collagen production and the connective tissue throughout your whole body, so it causes multisystemic problems," she said.

Although disability is rarely a subject heard in chart music, she believes there is value in writing openly about experiences that are often overlooked.

Asked whether that was part of her motivation, she replied: "Yes, I think so.

"Maybe part of that reason is because we're too ill to get to that level. The touring, the recording and everything that goes with it."

Her songs have long explored difficult subjects, including mental health and heartache, and she said audience members frequently tell her they recognise their own experiences in her lyrics.

"I did get a lot of people coming up to me after gigs and saying that they felt really seen and heard," she said.

"They've not really spoken openly about things that were affecting them, and they can see that someone else is able to do that."

Music has been at the centre of her life since childhood. Originally hailing from Tamworth, but now based in Shropshire, Rous has supported acts including Level 42 and Jamiroquai during her career, while continuing to write and perform original material.

Away from the stage, she has also spent the past eight years helping other artists find an audience through a songwriter showcase she runs at Albert's Shed in Shrewsbury.

But since undergoing spinal surgery in 2019, she said both her mobility and pain levels have worsened, making some aspects of performing increasingly difficult.

"It might be getting to the point where I will no longer be able to play music," she said.

"It's getting harder to play guitar. My voice, obviously, that's full of connective tissue, your vocal cords, so it's not what it used to be."

Despite that uncertainty, she remains determined to continue writing and performing for as long as possible.

"It's really just to get all these ideas out that I never recorded," she said.

"I will continue gigging [for] as long as I can."

For Rous, No Space Left is an attempt to shine a light on an experience that often goes unspoken. Through her music, she hopes people living with disability, chronic illness and isolation will feel, as she puts it, "not so alone".

articles.title: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Clayface’ lead sleepy Halloween weekend
articles.summary: The North American box office took a bit of a hit this weekend with the Halloween holiday drawing audiences away from theaters on Saturday.
articles.body: The North American box office took a bit of a hit this weekend with the Halloween holiday drawing audiences away from theaters on Saturday. Ticket sales were led by the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” and the DC Studios movie “Clayface,” and aren’t likely to surpass $56 million, according to studio estimates on Sunday. That would make it the second-lowest-earning weekend of the year. “You Can See Everything” had the slight edge over “Clayface,” with $10.6 million from 2,655 locations in its third weekend in theaters. The Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim-directed film has made $63.9 million to date against a reported production budget of $7 million and continues to generate the kind of buzz that’s hard to buy. This is the first time it’s hit No. 1, however. “Clayface,” about the Batman villain, trailed “You Can See Everything” by only $200,684. The Warner Bros. release fell 57% in its second weekend in theaters. That brings its domestic earnings to $44.1 million against a reported $44 million budget. Third place went to Laika’s animated film “Wildwood,” which added 150 screens in its second weekend, bringing its footprint to 3,100 theaters in the U.S. and Canada. The Fathom Entertainment release made an estimated $7.5 million, down 39% from its first weekend, bringing its running total to $25.9 million. The comedic fantasy “Wicker,” in which Olivia Colman plays a woman who commissions a basket maker to build her a wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård), landed in fourth place with $4.1 million. “Street Fighter,” now in its third weekend, rounded out the top five with $3.2 million. In notable expansions, the acclaimed Sundance indie “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” added over 1,000 locations in its second weekend and made $1.9 million, which landed it in the top 10. Netflix also reported earnings from the theatrical release of its World War II film “The Mosquito Bowl,” which made $455,000 from 349 locations. “La Bola Negra” made slightly less, $418,000, from only 38 locations in its third weekend, bringing its running total to $1.2 million. The domestic box office remains up over 17% from last year with nearly $8.5 billion to date. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “You Can See Everything,” $10.6 million. 2. “Clayface,” $10.4 million. 3. “Wildwood,” $7.5 million. 4. “Wicker,” $4.1 million. 5. “Street Fighter,” $3.2 million. 6. “Resident Evil,” $2.5 million. 7. “Other Mommy,” $2.5 million. 8. “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” $1.9 million. 9. “Heart of the Beast,” $1.6 million. 10. “Sense and Sensibility,” $1.4 million.

articles.summary: The makers of 'Hanuman Ansh' have issued a clarification regarding the film's ownership, rights and official representation, stating that no individual
articles.body: The makers of 'Hanuman Ansh' have issued a clarification regarding the film's ownership, rights and official representation, stating that no individual can independently claim authority to handle its affairs. Swambhu Media Network Pvt. Ltd. has emphasised that all decisions concerning the film must be taken in accordance with agreements signed between its producers. The statement also cautions against unauthorised transactions, public claims or commitments made using the film's name.Based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, popularly known as Maharaj ji, 'Hanuman Ansh' has four officially recognised producers: Namrata G Singh, Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi, Ragini Sona and Anupriya Nagar. The production company has clarified that all rights associated with the project, including theatrical, OTT, television, music, gaming and licensing rights across India and international markets, are governed by agreements between these producers.The company has further stated that matters concerning the film's publicity, award nominations, commercial rights and business collaborations cannot be handled independently. Such decisions require the producers' approval and must be routed through the company's authorised channels. It has also made it clear that any agreements, public announcements or award-related claims made without the necessary consent will not be considered valid or binding.The statement read, “The Company is aware that an individual is representing themselves as authorised to deal with the rights in the Film. No individual holds that authority. All rights in the Film (theatrical, streaming, broadcast, music, gaming, licensing, etc.), in India and Internationally, are dealt with only through the process set out in the inter-se agreements executed amongst the Producers.”As part of the clarification, the production house has designated Namrata G Singh and Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi as the film's sole Executive Directors. They will be responsible for overseeing public relations, marketing, awards and strategic partnerships, ensuring that all official communication and decisions are handled through a single authorised team.The makers have also issued guidelines for the film's cast and crew, stating that they must obtain prior approval before participating in any public engagement related to the project. This includes media interviews, podcasts, YouTube shows and other promotional appearances. Those interested in such engagements have been asked to contact the authorised representatives and secure formal confirmation beforehand.Reiterating its position, the company stated, “No party acting alone has authority to deal in the Film. Any such dealing is invalid and not binding on the Company or the Producers. Any statement, award claim or business arrangement made outside this process is not recognised by the Company. Those who engage outside it do so entirely at their own risk.”Explaining the need to safeguard the film's identity and association with Maharaj ji, Executive Directors Namrata G Singh and Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi said, “Hanuman Ansh belongs to Maharaj ji’s devotees across the world. Our duty is to protect it, and to give every partner one clear and verified door to the Film.”Swambhu Media Network has also warned that it will pursue appropriate action across territories against anyone attempting to misuse the film's name, credits or intellectual property.The clarification comes after 'Hanuman Ansh' reportedly registered an impressive theatrical run at the box office. Made on a reported budget of Rs 2 crore, the film has earned Rs 342.44 crore in net collections in India and Rs 452.86 crore worldwide, according to figures shared by Sacnilk. These figures account for its 87-day theatrical run. Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, the film is based on his book 'Divine Detour: That Changed My Life'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Heidi Klum's Halloween costume may have exposed secrets about 'The Batman Part II'
articles.summary: Fans spotted possible clues about the movie's villains in a post showing how Klum's severed-hand Halloween costume was made.
articles.body:
Clues about the villains in Robert Pattinson's upcoming Batman sequel may have been accidentally revealed in an Instagram post about Heidi Klum's Halloween costume.

The supermodel dressed as a giant, gruesome severed hand for Halloween, complete with replicas of her wedding rings — and a behind-the-scenes post showing the costume's creation appears to reveal objects linked to several Batman villains.

Eagle-eyed social media users spotted the items in what is reportedly the workspace of special effects makeup artist Mike Marino, who created Klum's costume and previously worked on 2022's The Batman and its HBO spinoff, The Penguin .

Among the objects visible was a facial cast that fans said resembled actor Brian Tyree Henry with a disfigured lip. Some connected it to Two-Face, a Batman villain who was once Gotham City's district attorney, Harvey Dent, before an attack left half his face disfigured.

The image also showed a box labeled "Zsasz." Victor Zsasz is the name of a serial killer from the comics who carves tally marks into his skin for each person he kills.

The post has renewed speculation about Sebastian Stan's role in the upcoming film. In June, entertainment journalist Jeff Sneider reported that Stan would play Zsasz in The Batman Part II , while Henry would portray Harvey Dent / Two-Face. Neither casting claim has been officially confirmed.

Another box was labeled "Owl 3," which fans have speculated could refer to the Court of Owls, a secret society that influences Gotham City in DC Comics.

Marino confirmed his involvement in The Batman Part II in an October interview with W magazine , adding to speculation that the objects could be connected to the sequel. "To be honest, I'm a comic book nerd, so the fact that I'm working on [ The Batman: Part II ] is a dream scenario," he said. "We're doing some really cool makeup in this new movie, so that's the dream right there."

However, none of the apparent clues have been confirmed to belong to the new movie, and there is no indication that the objects were deliberately included in the Halloween post as hints about it. Yahoo has contracted Marino for comment.

Director Matt Reeves confirmed Henry and Stan's involvement in the sequel in May but did not reveal which characters they would play. Variety said Stan was "set to play" Harvey Dent.

Stan told the Happy Sad Confused podcast in an episode released in October that the movie is "going to be great," adding, "This is definitely, for me, feeling like something very different than I've gotten to do. And that's what I love, and I'm excited about."

The Batman Part II is scheduled to hit theaters on Feb. 18, 2028. It was originally due for release in October 2025 but was delayed by the Hollywood strikes.

Production was temporarily halted last month as Reeves stepped away for personal reasons . Ocean's Eleven director Steven Soderbergh was hired to help finish filming. The original movie was released in March 2022.

articles.title: Imran Khan apologises as Bombay High Court slams the actor for participating in protests despite being an OCI card holder: 'If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated?'
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for participating in a protest
articles.body: The Bombay High Court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for participating in a protest related to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) issue in Mumbai. The court observed that the fundamental right to protest is reserved for Indian citizens, following which the actor tendered an unconditional apology and assured the bench that he would not participate in any such demonstration in the future.A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna observed that India's magnanimity was evident from the fact that Khan, despite being a US citizen, was first served a notice asking him to leave the country rather than being deported immediately.Appearing for Khan, senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond promptly submitted an undertaking on behalf of the 43-year-old actor, assuring the court that he would neither participate in protests in the future nor encourage anyone else to do so. He also tendered an unconditional apology.The court subsequently scheduled Khan's petition challenging the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) notice for further hearing on December 7. The notice had directed him to leave India by October 28 over his alleged participation in a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Mumbai last month. The bench also extended its earlier order keeping the FRRO notice in abeyance until the next hearing.During the proceedings, the court maintained that an OCI cardholder does not enjoy the same rights as an Indian citizen, particularly when it comes to participating in protests. Drawing a comparison with how foreign nationals are treated in other countries, the bench remarked, "If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated? If this had happened in America, the person would have been put on the next flight back to India,"The judges also suggested that Khan consider applying for Indian citizenship if he wished to participate in demonstrations concerning issues affecting Indian citizens. While the bench acknowledged that the authorities were within their sovereign powers to issue the notice, it also urged them to consider the circumstances before taking further action."He (Khan) is ready to tender an unconditional apology. He has been in India since childhood. Show some magnanimity and a big heart now. We have to be 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family)," the court observed.At the same time, the judges made it clear that the actor could not take his OCI status for granted. Referring to the powers available to the government under the law, the bench said, "As an OCI cardholder, you (Khan) are at the mercy of this country. Hence, such behaviour cannot be tolerated, but one chance can be given," the HC said. The court also questioned Khan's reason for attending a demonstration concerning an issue linked to Indian electoral processes. Asking what connection the actor had with the SIR exercise, the bench remarked that he had no right to participate in a protest concerning Indian citizens."For what had he (Khan) gone to a place of protest (in Mumbai)?" the judges asked, adding in a lighter vein that the actor did not even have an upcoming film to promote. "The rights Indian citizens enjoy and the rights available to OCI cardholders are different. If he had been an Indian citizen then the situation would have been different," Chief Justice Tripathi noted.Reiterating its position, the bench added that Khan's OCI status did not entitle him to exercise the same privileges as an Indian citizen. "You (Khan) had no right to participate in a protest of such nature. You have no connection with the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls undertaken by EC). The right to protest is not available to an OCI cardholder," the HC said.The judges further took note of Khan's social media activity following his release from police detention, observing that his posts could influence his young followers."Your social media posts (after he was released from detention by police) amounted to instigation. You have young followers who are bound to get influenced," the court said.The FRRO issued the 'Leave India' notice under Sections 7(2)(C) and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, provisions that empower the government to regulate the movement of foreign nationals and order their removal from the country. Khan was directed to leave India by October 28, failing which deportation proceedings could be initiated.The action followed his brief detention by Mumbai Police during a demonstration held on October 10 at the city's historic August Kranti Maidan. The protest was organised in solidarity with an agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls.In his petition challenging the FRRO's decision, filed through advocate Zulfiquar Memon, Khan maintained that he had neither participated in the gathering nor had any association or affiliation with its organisers.Describing the notice as "illegal, arbitrary, perverse and drastic," the actor alleged that the authorities had failed to apply their minds before targeting him because of his public profile. He further argued that the action amounted to "patent non-application of mind and the arbitrary targeting" of a public figure.The petition also contended, "Not only is the notice manifestly disproportionate, if implemented, it would reduce the very principles of natural justice that the authorities are duty-bound to uphold, to nothing but a dead letter."Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Years before making Rs 400 crore 'Ramayana', Namit Malhotra mortgaged house to invest Rs 7 lakh into VFX business, took Rs 2 crore loan from bank: 'We would have become homeless'
articles.summary: Ever since Ranbir Kapoor-starrer 'Ramayana' was announced, producer Namit Malhotra has been at the centre of curiosity, with many wondering about the man
articles.body: Ever since Ranbir Kapoor-starrer 'Ramayana' was announced, producer Namit Malhotra has been at the centre of curiosity, with many wondering about the man backing one of Indian cinema's most ambitious projects, reportedly mounted on a budget of Rs 4,000 crore. A third-generation member of a film family, Namit's journey to becoming a filmmaker was far from conventional. He started his entrepreneurial journey at just 18, built a visual effects company from scratch and even saw his family home being mortgaged to keep his dream alive. His ultimate ambition was always to make a film on a scale that could compete with the best in the world.Namit's association with cinema goes back generations. His grandfather, MN Malhotra, began his career as a cameraman and went on to shoot 'Jhansi Ki Rani', regarded as the first Indian film shot in colour. His father, Naresh Malhotra, also ventured into film production and backed projects such as 'Shahenshah'. Growing up in a family immersed in filmmaking, Namit naturally developed aspirations of becoming a director.In an old interview with Komal Nahta on ETC, recorded nearly 15 years ago, Namit spoke about his early ambitions and how he eventually found his way into the world of visual effects.“I wanted to become a filmmaker. I was extremely focused growing up to become a director and make films. Around that time, my father started a new business. So it seemed like a good opportunity to fill the technological gap in our industry.”Recalling a conversation with his father when he turned 18, Namit said, “After turning 18, I was asked by my father what I wanted to do career-wise. I was not a very studious child. I didn’t enjoy studying, so I told him there are two things I don’t want to do. I don’t want to do your business, and I hate computers. Barring these two, advise me anything.”Namit later explained that he had intentionally ruled out the two career paths he thought his father might suggest, as his own interest lay in becoming a film director. However, an unexpected conversation during a flight introduced him to the possibilities of computer graphics and changed his professional trajectory.“I bumped into my father’s friend on a flight when he asked me what I wanted to do. It was during this conversation that I told him, ‘I want to become a film director, but my father wants me to take up computer graphics.’ The friend told me that computer graphics is like filmmaking. I got fascinated, but I am not good at drawing.”Intrigued by the idea, Namit enrolled in a computer graphics course, although the experience did not go quite as planned.“It was a three-month course. I believe in shortcuts. The instructor tried to teach me, but I couldn’t get interested. At the same time, there were some developments in post-production, and an opportunity came up to offer computer-based editing services.”Instead of pursuing the course further, Namit joined hands with the instructors and started a business out of a garage. The venture was established with an initial investment of around Rs 7 lakh, partly funded by his father and partly through a bank loan. Recalling those early days, he said, “None of us had any experience. I was 19, they were 21. We invested about Rs 7 lakh. My father funded some of it, and the rest was a loan from the bank.”The small garage operation gradually developed into a full-fledged studio. As the business expanded, the team rented apartments within the same building to accommodate its growing operations. By 2006, the company had established a presence across India.Namit has often credited his father for backing his ideas without questioning his ambitions. Recalling the unwavering support he received, he said, “I would only tell him, ‘I want to do this,’ and he would be like, ‘Then go do it.’ He even said, ‘I will put the house on the line, mortgage it.'”That faith came with considerable financial risk. At one point, the family home had to be mortgaged to secure funding for the business. Reflecting on the decision and the stakes involved, Namit said, “In 1997, I knew there was no bigger risk than this. My company’s turnover was Rs 75 lakh, and the loan we had taken was Rs 2 crore. I knew that if the business failed, our story would have been completely finished. After all, it was a new technology. We would have become homeless, as we had invested everything in it. I was 21. But without flinching, my father did it, maybe because I am his only son.”Apart from taking financial risks, Namit also built his company around the belief that talent and dedication mattered more than formal qualifications. He has maintained that a person's willingness to learn and passion for the craft were more important than their educational background. Citing an example from his own team, he said, “The boy who delivered chai to our team is now a core part of our team. Today, he is one of the most well-respected creative technicians in our company. He is very well-regarded in the industry.”Over the last three decades, Namit has transformed his venture into a globally recognised visual effects company, contributing to several Hollywood productions, including 'Avatar'. With eight Oscars associated with its work and achievements, the company has built a formidable reputation in the international film industry.Having spent years developing the technological expertise and resources required to execute large-scale cinematic projects, Namit is now backing his long-held ambition with 'Ramayana'. The Rs 4,000-crore epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, marks a significant milestone in a journey that began with a teenager determined to make films, even if he had to take an unconventional route to get there.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2016, Dakota Johnson bought her first permanent Los Angeles home for $3.55 million with her ‘Fifty Shades of Grey’ earnings; decade later, the actress sold the mid-century modern house for $5.924 million after making it her own with designer updates
articles.summary: Dakota Johnson has sold the mid-century modern house in Los Angeles that she called home for a decade.
articles.body: Dakota Johnson has sold the mid-century modern house in Los Angeles that she called home for a decade. The three-bedroom property on Marmont Avenue, with its clean lines and views of the Chateau Marmont, closed for $5.924 million in June 2026 according to Mansion Global. She had bought it in 2016 for $3.55 million, with her payout from the first instalment of the ‘Fifty Shades of Grey’ trilogy, the actress told Architectural Digest. “I thought it would be healthy to have a base,” she said. “And, at the very least, have one place where you know your stuff is, as opposed to 10 places.” The sale marks the end of a chapter in a house she once described as a place to finally put down roots, and the beginning of a new one in the Hollywood Hills.A quick sale of Dakota Johnson’s house after a short listingJohnson listed the house for $6 million and it moved fast according to Realtor.com. Within days it went under contract, and the final price came in just under the asking figure at $5.924 million. The 3,210-square-foot home sits on a gated, terraced lot and had become well known for its mid-century design, large glass walls, and thoughtful updates. After nearly ten years of ownership, the sale delivered a clear gain over the original purchase price.Dakota Johnson’s house designed by Carl MastonThe house was built in 1947 by architect Carl Maston, a name associated with California modernism. It mixes timber, concrete, and wood-framed glass in the classic mid-century style. Three matching wooden doors mark the front, and a sliding door opens straight to the swimming pool. The terraced grounds include gardens, lawns, and an outdoor fire pit, giving the place a quiet, tree-house feel even though it sits above the Sunset Strip.Pierce & Ward’s soft updates on Dakota Johnson’s residenceJohnson brought in the design firm Pierce & Ward to refresh the interiors. The kitchen became a talking point after she showed the house to Architectural Digest. In the primary suite they created a custom pink bathroom inspired by a sweater from The Row. Glass walls open the rooms to the backyard and pool, keeping the indoor-outdoor flow that defines the original architecture while adding a warmer, more personal layer.From first permanent home to a new chapterWhen Johnson bought the house in 2016, she was clear about her reason. “I wanted a place to put all my stuff,” she told Architectural Digest at the time. It was her first real base after years of moving around. Before the sale she had already moved into a different property in the Outpost Estates area of the Hollywood Hills, a Mediterranean-style house she purchased for about $5.3 million, she talked about it in an interview with Vogue. She has spoken about loving the views of olive trees and sky there, and the sense of privacy it offers “With my job and the velocity at which my schedule can change, it’s important for me to have a place to go to and it be mine,” she says. “Psychologically, I’m moored somewhere. This place is my anchor”, she said.About Dakota JohnsonDakota Johnson is an American actress who first became widely known for the ‘Fifty Shades’ films and has since built a varied career across independent and studio projects. The daughter of actors Melanie Griffith and Don Johnson, she has appeared in films such as ‘The Lost Daughter’, ‘Persuasion’, and ‘Materialists’, earning praise for her understated style and range. articles.title: Jack Lowden says James Bond speculation is 'flattering'
articles.summary: The Slow Horses star is among three actors reported to be in the running for the iconic movie role.
articles.body:
Slow Horses star Jack Lowden has described the speculation he could be the next James Bond as "flattering".

The 36-year-old - who grew up in Oxton in the Scottish Borders - has been reported to be in the running for the role alongside Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor.

The actor chosen will replace Daniel Craig, who took over the role of Bond with Casino Royale in 2006 and bowed out after his fifth film, No Time To Die, in 2021.

Speaking to GQ Hype , Lowden responded to the rumours - but did not confirm or deny whether he was part of the auditioning process.

Jack Lowden makes appearance in old school's show

"On this… it's all very flattering," he said.

"It's nice to be mentioned – for any role – and I'm just not really going to add to the noise," he said.

Last month, his Slow Horses co-star Gary Oldman claimed the new Bond had been chosen, adding that he had his "fingers crossed" for Lowden.

Speaking to Canada's Global, Oldman said: "It's been rumoured that he's on the shortlist.

"We're going to find out pretty soon, aren't we? Because they have picked him.

"They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack."

When asked about Oldman's comments, Lowden said: "It's very nice, and Gary's a sweetheart – it's particularly lovely, coming from someone like him.

He added: "As a young male actor, generally, the minute you're not playing a zany artist type, the minute you're in a suit, people fling it at you."

During an appearance at the Toronto International Film Festival, Oldman clarified his remarks and said he had only heard a rumour that producers had selected an actor from a shortlist, not that Lowden had been cast.

He said he did not know who had got the part but he was hoping it was his co-star.

Lowden is best known for his roles in films including Dunkirk and Mary Queen Of Scots, as well as TV roles in Slow Horses and War and Peace.

The actor has also been awarded two Baftas and a Laurence Olivier Award as well as nominations for two Primetime Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe Award.

He is next starring alongside Emma Corrin in Dolly Alderton's adaptation of Pride And Prejudice.

The next Bond film is in development after it was announced last year that Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight would write the script.

Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce the upcoming project, which is currently untitled, while Dune's Denis Villeneuve will direct.

Pascal told Deadline earlier this year that a casting announcement by the end of the year was a "good bet" but that Craig was a "hard act to follow".

articles.summary: Ranchi Municipal Corporation deploys 1,200 workers and lighting teams to clean 72 Chhath ghats, with zonal monitoring, safety barricades and helpline support.
articles.body: Ranchi: More than 1,200 sanitation workers and 25 special lighting teams have been deployed across 72 ghats in run up to the Chhath festival scheduled in the second week of November, the Ranchi Municipal Corporation (RMC) said in a statement issued on Monday.“The ghats have been divided into eight zones and officials assigned to monitor preparations and address issues on the ground. articles.title: 'Homestead' star Bailey Chase says California vaccine plans were 'final straw' that drove family out of LA
articles.summary: Bailey Chase reveals the proposed COVID-19 vaccine mandate that drove his family from California to the mountains of North Carolina five years ago.
articles.body: "Homestead" star Bailey Chase is opening up about the "final straw" that drove him and his family out of California for a new life in North Carolina. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old actor, who shares daughter Waverly, 12, and 10-year-old twins Maggie and Gauge with his wife Amy, explained that concerns over how California's COVID-19 restrictions would impact his children led him to leave the Golden State behind. "That happened five years ago in the throes of COVID," Chase said. "My wife and I picked up sticks with our three young children when they were mandating vaccines out there." "They said they couldn't go back to school without it," Chase, who stars as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in "Homestead," continued. "And that was the final straw. And we've been in the mountains of North Carolina ever since living our best life." ZACHARY LEVI SAYS TEXAS GIVES HIM THE ‘FREEDOM’ HE COULDN’T FIND IN CALIFORNIA Five years after trading Los Angeles for North Carolina, Chase told Fox News Digital that his life now largely revolves around his children's activities when he isn't working. 'VIRGIN RIVER' STAR BEN HOLLINGSWORTH SAYS HIS KIDS HAVE FREEDOM IN SMALL TOWN THAT 'DOESN'T FLY' IN LA "I'm like soccer dad right now. It's soccer season, so we're going here and there," he said. "My oldest is really into ballet, and I couldn't be more proud of her and getting ready for ‘The Nutcracker’ in December, and basketball season's around the corner." While Chase remains committed to his acting career, the "Longmire" alum said his priorities shift completely when he returns home. CHRIS PRATT SAYS HIS FAITH WILL BE 'THE MOST IMPORTANT THING' THAT HE PASSES ON TO HIS KIDS "I love my job, and when I'm off filming, I'm 100% focused on that. But when I'm home, I'm home," he said. "There's no greater job than being a dad." Chase and his family currently live in Amy's hometown of Hendersonville in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Western North Carolina, about 25 miles south of Asheville. Chase has previously explained that Amy had long envisioned eventually returning to the area where she was born and raised. The actor also has ties to North Carolina after attending Duke University in Durham on a football scholarship. 'RANSOM CANYON' STAR JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HE'D RATHER PUT MONEY INTO NORTH DAKOTA AFTER SELLING LOS ANGELES HOME "Amy, being from the mountains of North Carolina, always had it in the back of her mind that she’d go back home one day," he said in a January 2026 interview with Duke Alumni Magazine. "We didn’t know how or when." However, Chase recalled they decided the time was right due to California's handling of the pandemic. ‘TWILIGHT’ STAR KELLAN LUTZ TRADED CALIFORNIA FOR TENNESSEE LAND AND BIBLE STUDIES "Things started to not work in LA during COVID – they shut down the schools, there were no sports for the kids," he said. "Really, no life, no work. And it became more and more obvious that we should leave LA." "Amy’s very close with her parents, who are in N.C.," he continued. "Everything’s about seven minutes away: school, the in-laws, the grocery store, golf course, soccer field. It’s a great location. We live in a house that would not have been affordable in LA." JANA KRAMER SAYS LOS ANGELES PRICED HER OUT OF THE CHILDHOOD SHE WANTED FOR HER KIDS "It’s a kid’s dream," he added. "There’s a sports court and a pool. We have two golden retriever puppies, so it’s a full and lively house." During a February appearance on the "Undaunted.Life: A Man's Podcast," Chase elaborated on the concerns that he had over California's proposed vaccine mandate for his young children's return to school. "At that time, you know, they're 4, 4 and 6 years old," he recalled. "I got two young girls and, you know we don't need to go down that rabbit hole." "I was like, 'No, I just don't know enough,'" he continued. "And I got one job right now, and it's to take care of these little nuggets. That's the most important job I have right now." In October 2021, California Gov. articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor has drawn a comparison between Elon Musk’s flying car technology and the aerial chariot Pushpak Viman from the ‘Ramayana’, saying India achieved this feat thousands of years ago. The actor, who plays Lord Ram in the new adaptation of Valmiki’s epic, made the remark while promoting the film.Ranbir’s remark on flying carsMusk unveiled the redesigned, next-generation Tesla Roadster on October 15. The car features rocket-inspired air thrusters developed with SpaceX. According to the PTI report, speaking on a chat show hosted by TV presenter Suma, the ‘Animal’ actor said, “Elon Musk recently invented a flying car; I think India did it 5000 years back.” His co-stars Yash, Ravie Dubey and Rakul Preet Singh, along with director Nitesh Tiwari, also joined the interview.How the Pushpak Viman was designedTiwari said the team went through 40 to 50 designs before finalising the lotus-shaped Pushpak Viman seen in the film. In the story, Ravana flies in it after abducting Sita and taking her to Lanka.He added that the final look was very different from what the team first imagined, which meant the Ravana and Jatayu fight had to be reworked many times. “It took us so long to shape the Ravana and Jatayu fight. Because previously, we assumed the design of Pushpak Viman would be something different, and we shaped the sequence around it. And when we loved the final design, which was completely different from what we had first thought, we had to do a lot of iterations,” he said.Explaining the thinking behind the design, he said, “We created some 40-50 designs for Pushpak Viman before finalising the one you see in the film. We didn’t want something that did look like it could fly; we wanted some kind of science to go into it. Because I believe, we all believe, there was science behind everything that happened that time.”About ‘Ramayana’‘Ramayana’ is planned as a two-part cinematic adaptation of one of India’s most revered epics. articles.standfirst: La cantante ha hecho una parada en el país azteca para vivir desde dentro esta popular tradición
articles.summary: La cantante ha hecho una parada en el país azteca para vivir desde dentro esta popular tradición
articles.body: Aitana ha compartido unas fotos donde luce la indumentaria y el característico maquillaje blanco de calavera tradicionales para sumergirse de lleno en la celebración del Día de los Muertos en México. Con un atuendo que el punto de color lo aporta unas flores amarillas y un cuidado diseño inspirado en las emblemáticas Catrinas mexicanas, la artista catalana ha mostrado su fascinación y respeto por la cultura mexicana, enamorando a millones de seguidores que no han tardado en llenar su publicación de mensajes. Estas imágenes llegan en un punto clave de su trayecto internacional, pues la cantante aterriza en tierras mexicanas tras completar una exitosa fase de su gira por América. Su paso por el continente ha estado lleno de momentos memorables, teniendo como última parada una serie de multitudinarios conciertos en Argentina. En recintos abarrotados como el Movistar Arena de Buenos Aires, la intérprete logró conectar profundamente con el público rioplatense, consolidando una de las etapas más vibrantes de su tour. Lejos de tomarse un descanso, la agenda de la artista continúa a un ritmo vertiginoso con sus próximos compromisos en directo. Aitana ofrecerá una seguidilla de conciertos en distintas ciudades de México, incluyendo paradas en Guadalajara, Querétaro, Puebla y múltiples noches consecutivas en el prestigioso Auditorio Nacional de la Ciudad de México. Posteriormente, la gira cruzará la frontera a finales de mes para desembarcar en Estados Unidos, con actuaciones programadas en emblemáticos escenarios de Nueva York y Miami. La festividad del Día de los Muertos, que ha servido de inspiración para las fotos de la cantante, es una de las tradiciones más sinceras y arraigadas de la cultura mexicana. Declarada Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad por la UNESCO, esta celebración —que tiene lugar entre el 1 y el 2 de noviembre— no se vive desde el duelo o la tristeza, sino como un alegre reencuentro temporal entre los vivos y las almas de sus seres queridos fallecidos. A través de vistosos altares con ofrendas llenas de flores de cempasúchil, comida, veladoras y música, las familias honran el recuerdo de quienes ya no están, recordando que la memoria es el único puente capaz de vencer a la muerte.

articles.title: Bill Murray Asks Trump’s Top Economic Adviser to Say ‘My Dog Just Died’ to Wipe Smile Off His Face in Bizarre Exchange on CNBC
articles.summary: Actor and comedian Bill Murray apparently had had enough of the grinning mug of Kevin Hassett, Trump’s top economic adviser, in a weird impromptu exchange on...
articles.body:
Actor and comedian Bill Murray apparently had had enough of the grinning mug of Kevin Hassett, Trump's top economic adviser, in a weird impromptu exchange on CNBC's "Squawk Box" program.

Murray unexpectedly inserted himself into a CNBC interview Monday between "Squawk Box" hosts Joe Kernan and Becky Quick and Hassett, who serves as National Economic Council director, in a segment about the state of the economy. In the middle of the interview, Murray appeared between the show's hosts and asked Hassett (who appeared on camera remotely) to say the words, "My dog just died."

Murray, after being introduced by Kernan, said that "I would regret it if I didn't take this opportunity." He then asked Hassett, who recently called the affordability crisis in the U.S. a "myth": "Could you just say the words, 'My dog just died?' I want to see what happens to your smile."

Hassett queried, "Oh, well, is it your dog or my dog?" "Your dog," Murray said. "OK. My dog just died," Hassett said, without smiling. Exclaimed Kernan, "You did it!"

Murray then told Hassett, "We were gonna have someone go take your blood. We're gonna call them off. Not gonna happen."

Murray was in CNBC's studios after he had appeared on "Squawk Box" earlier Monday for an interview together with author Tom Coyne about "A Course Called Ireland," a six-part travel and golf docuseries on Paramount+ he stars in that's based Coyne's 2009 book of the same name.

Hassett was in the news last week when he called the "affordability crisis" in the U.S. a "myth" that was being promoted by Trump-haters. "The amount of consumption per household has gone up maybe around $5,000 per household," Hassett told Fox Business' Larry Kudlow, per Mediaite . "That's after inflation, because of the income boom, the capital spending boom, the fact that people aren't losing their jobs, all the things that have made the economy great means that [the] affordability crisis — it's a myth!"

articles.summary: Bill Murray crashed a live CNBC interview with Kevin Hassett, one of President Donald Trump’s top economic advisers, asking him to say, “My dog just died.”
articles.body: Oscar-nominated actor Bill Murray crashed a live CNBC interview Monday with one of President Donald Trump’s top economic advisers, poking fun at the official’s perpetual grin. Murray, who appeared on CNBC’s “Squawk Box” to promote a new streaming series, took aim at Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council. “Why is that man always smiling? I’m a little concerned,” Murray said. “Not worried. Concerned.” Hassett was scheduled to join “Squawk Box” co-anchors Joe Kernen and Becky Quick via satellite from the White House. Murray inserted herself into the interview from the show’s set in Manhattan. “I would regret it if I didn’t take this opportunity. Could you just say the words, ‘My dog just died’? I want to see what happens to your smile,” Murray said to Hassett. “Well,” Hassett replied with a laugh, “is it your dog or my dog?” “Your dog,” Murray said. “Okay,” Hassett said with a frown. “My dog just died.” Murray dropped by “Squawk Box” with author Tom Coyne to promote their new Paramount+ travel series “A Course Called Ireland,” a guide to the golf courses of Ireland. The six-part documentary series debuted Oct. 25. CNBC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the exchange between Murray and Hassett. The former “Saturday Night Live” cast member is a longtime CNBC viewer who has appeared on the cable channel’s shows in the past. He is also a Berkshire Hathaway shareholder who has attended the company’s annual meetings.

articles.title: From Nancy Kerrigan to Jackie Kennedy: Jessica Alba, Martha Stewart and more celebrity Halloween costumes that sparked backlash
articles.summary: Some stars missed the mark with their costumes — and have since deleted their Instagram posts.
articles.body:
Halloween has come and gone — but some celebrities are still facing backlash for their costumes. This year, A-listers got creative with their looks and received plenty of praise (see: Heidi Klum dressing up as her own severed hand and Harry Styles poking fun at his X Factor -era style ). Unfortunately, not every celebrity's getup was well received.

Case in point? A handful of stars, including Martha Stewart and Jessica Alba, initially shared their 2026 Halloween costumes on Instagram — but deleted the posts after drawing criticism from commenters.

Jessica Alba dressed up as Nancy Kerrigan — the former American figure skater who was assaulted weeks before the 1994 Winter Olympics — and the backlash was almost immediate. In a since-deleted carousel of photos shared on Nov. 1, Alba wore a white lace figure skating dress with a bloody bandage wrapped around her knee. Alba's friend dressed up as Tonya Harding, Kerrigan's former skating rival, and posed with a baseball bat.

"Happy Halloween from Tonya … and Nancy," Alba captioned the post.

The duo's costume directly references the 1994 attack on Kerrigan, who was struck on the knee with a police baton following a practice skate at the U.S. Figure Skating Championships in Detroit. The attacker, Shane Stant, was hired by Jeff Gillooly, Harding's ex-husband, and Shawn Eckhardt, Gillooly's childhood friend. Harding, who denied she planned the attack, pleaded guilty to conspiring to hinder the prosecution. She received probation and a life ban from the U.S. Figure Skating Association.

"Immature," one commenter wrote, according to Page Six . "We expect better, Jessica."

"Explain what's funny about a woman being beaten up. I'll wait," another added.

Martha Stewart shared a since-deleted photo of herself on Oct. 31 dressed as an unhoused person. She wore tattered clothing and makeup resembling dirt on her face while holding a clipboard that read, "I am hungry. Help me!!"

Stewart — whose net worth is worth hundreds of millions of dollars — addressed the backlash over her costume. In a statement shared with People on Nov. 1, the beloved television personality said her outfit was "intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness." Stewart said she is "distressed" that the costume "offended" people.

"Homelessness continues to remain one of America's greatest challenges and ongoing crises, something that I care deeply about and I have spent a significant amount of time and effort supporting charities that combat this ongoing social epidemic. I am committed to continuing to make a difference," she wrote.

Stewart shared another statement on Instagram, writing, "It's hard to admit when you've really screwed up. My earlier statement didn't go far enough."

McCall DaPron, star of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, which premieres on Nov. 12, channeled Jackie Kennedy for her Halloween 2026 costume. On Oct. 30, DaPron shared a photo of herself with her husband, Kirk DaPron, and their four children dressed up as the Kennedy family on the day of President John F. Kennedy's assassination.

"Happy Halloween 🩷The Kennedy's," DaPron, who wore Kennedy's recognizable pink suit, wrote alongside the since-deleted snap. The reality star turned off comments on the Instagram post before eventually deleting it.

Commenters called DaPron out for being "appalling and distasteful," according to People .

"[You're] dressing up as a woman on the scariest day of her life…," another wrote, per the outlet.

Julia Fox faced similar backlash for her 2025 Halloween costume, when she dressed up as the former first lady moments after President Kennedy's assassination. The Uncut Gems actor wore a bloodied pink suit, which she defended as being a statement rather than a costume.

"[Jackie Kennedy's] decision not to change clothes, even after being encouraged to, was an act of extraordinary bravery," Fox wrote. "It was performance, protest, and mourning all at once. A woman weaponizing image and grace to expose brutality."

articles.title: Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce’s Marriage Reportedly Faces New Update After Reports She Was ‘Furious’ Over a Wedding ‘Betrayal’
articles.summary: How is the power couple doing?
articles.body:
Despite a recent wedding "betrayal," Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are reportedly thriving in their marriage.

An insider recently told The Daily Mail that Swift and Kelce have "happily adjusted to life as husband and wife," revealing that they often work out and prepare protein-filled meals together.

"They work out a ton together," the source said. "They love to lift weights and stay strong, and they stick to a lean diet. There is a lot of protein in their meals."

Swifties know the "Love Story" singer's a baking enthusiast, but these days, she's "eased off" the sweets because Kelce "needs to be in the best shape of his life" for the NFL season. Still, she'll make her husband's "favorite" meal, French toast, once in a while.

Elsewhere in the interview, the insider indicated that Swift couldn't be happier in her marriage to Kelce. The global pop star has reportedly been telling her close friends that "she loves being Mrs. Kelce and loves saying she is a married woman. She has found the one."

The billionaire has also been working on "finding the balance between work and married life," and she's allegedly planning her next move. According to the insider, Swift has been writing constantly—and she likely has enough new material for two new albums: "Taylor takes notes, hums new melodies and reads a lot of books for inspiration."

But for now, Swift is excited to be by Kelce's side and cheer him and the Kansas City Chiefs on every week. The source added that she "does everything to support him because he is working so hard on football."

Even though some WAGs struggle with their partner's grueling football schedule, Swift is nothing but supportive. "She accepts that Travis has to commit so much time to the Chiefs," the source explained. "She never complains because football is his passion. He has been in practice since August, so he has been hyper-focused for a long time."

This latest update on their marriage comes shortly after Swift was said to be livid over their wedding photos leaking online. In late October 2026, The Daily Mail published photos from inside Swift and Kelce's New York City wedding.

"Taylor was furious because this was supposed to be a tightly controlled, private celebration," one insider told celebrity expert Rob Shuter . "Everyone had been told to keep quiet, and the NDAs were there for a reason. She never expected those images to get out."

Another insider shared that Swift is heartbroken, noting, "When you go to extraordinary lengths to protect your privacy, a leak like this feels like a betrayal. It makes you question who you can trust and whether anything can truly remain private anymore."

Now, the couple will likely never release their official photos publicly. The leak has done a lot of damage, and Swift is apparently deeply upset that photos from her and Kelce's big day were posted without their consent.

Mi mujer me hablaba y me costaba contestar, reaccionar. Me fui a la cama y, cuando me desperté a la mañana siguiente, tenía medio cuerpo dormido, no quería pensar que me iba a castigar la vida con otro ictus y quise quitarle importancia. Me subí al avión y con la presión me pegó el ictus fortísimo, no podía ni caminar. Todavía me quedan algunas secuelas, que no son visibles, pero internamente estoy jodido. PABLO MOTOS. Dices que en este segundo ictus lo bueno es que tenías a tu madre. KIKO RIVERA. Sentía frio, silencio, la oscuridad, pero esta vez tenía el abrazo de mi madre, llevábamos seis años sin hablarnos. Malditos seis años. Yo ahora me cuido más, he dejado de fumar y no bebo nada de alcohol, pero no me he convertido de repente en un niño de San Ildefonso, sigo siendo Kiko Rivera. Es que a mí me gusta todo lo malo, no lo puedo evitar, me gusta mucho comer y mi absoluta debilidad es la Coca-Cola. Soy diabético tipo 2, hipertenso, tengo colesterol, ácido úrico y me han dado dos ictus con 42 años. PABLO MOTOS. Creo que el neurólogo te ha obligado a pasar también menos horas delante de la pantalla. KIKO RIVERA. Sí, yo venía haciendo 100 shows al año y en casa también trabajo con el ordenador delante. El neurólogo ahora me obliga solo a estar ciertas horas al día delante de las pantallas y no seguidas. Son muchos cambios los que estoy haciendo, poco a poco. PABLO MOTOS. Cuéntanos cuando te llamó Cristiano Ronaldo. KIKO RIVERA. Es uno de los momentos más míticos de mi vida. Yo estaba en 'Gran Hermano' y llegué a la final. Me llamó el que era en ese momento portero del Sevilla, que era amigo mío para felicitarme, y me dijo que si le podía pasar mi número a Cristiano Ronaldo, que se lo había pedido. Le dije que claro y me pasé una semana sin dormir bien, pendiente del móvil por si me llamaba, pensando que me iba a dar la oportunidad de mi vida. Un día, estaba durmiendo la siesta y me despertó una llamada de un número muy largo, no lo quería coger porque pensaba que era publicidad, pero insistía e insistía. Ya lo cogí y era Cristiano, yo pensaba que me quería contratar para una fiesta como DJ, pero me dijo que lo que quería era ponerme pelo, porque tiene una cadena de clínicas. Al final no cuajó la idea, porque yo no quería ponerme pelo y le pedí un millón de euros, pero no le debió parecer bien porque no me volvió a llamar.

articles.title: Bombay High Court grants 'Ramayana' dynamic injunction; order protects Rs 2,000 crore film from copyright infringement, unauthorised recording and streaming
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court on Monday granted a dynamic ad-interim injunction to protect the upcoming film 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' from copyright
articles.body: The Bombay High Court on Monday granted a dynamic ad-interim injunction to protect the upcoming film 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' from copyright infringement, restraining unidentified 'John Doe' entities and digital platforms from unauthorised recording, hosting, streaming or distributing the film ahead of its global theatrical release.The interim order was passed by Justice Madhav Jamdar in a suit filed by Godpower Media Private Limited, which holds the film's copyright and exploitation rights in the film after acquiring its domestic and territorial intellectual property rights. The suit sought protection for the film's underlying script, characters, footage, lyrics and recordings.Judge Madhav Jamdar passes order to protect filmAs reported by Bar and Bench, observing the potential threat of copyright infringement, Justice Jamdar noted, “Prima facie, the plaintiff (Godpower) has real and well-founded apprehension that the film or parts of it will be recorded and uploaded, streamed, or communicated to the public on various platforms.”'Ramayana' clips leaked despite non-disclosure agreementsDuring the proceedings, the court was informed that Part One of 'Ramayana' had been produced at a cost of Rs 2,000 Crore, with the combined budget for the two-part saga amounting to Rs 4,000 Crore. Godpower stated that despite strict non-disclosure obligations imposed during invite-only preview screenings, both trailers had been secretly recorded and circulated across digital platforms.The court's order includes a dynamic injunction against unidentified 'John Doe' entities, enabling action against infringers whose identities may not be known at the time of the proceedings. It also directs internet service providers (ISPs) and social media intermediaries to block or take down infringing links and mirror websites upon receiving written notice.Google LLC ordered to take down links infringing contentThe court further directed Godpower to share the URLs carrying unauthorised copies of the film with the relevant internet service providers and digital platforms, which must then take immediate steps to block access to, disable or remove the infringing content.Counsel representing Google LLC and global social media intermediaries recorded 'no objection' to the order and assured the court that they would 'act promptly' upon being notified of offending links.The matter is scheduled to be heard next on December 16.The order comes ahead of the film's global release on November 5. 'Ramayana', directed by Nitesh Tiwari, stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash in lead roles. articles.title: Justin Timberlake to Release Four-Part ‘Tell-All’ Docuseries, Featuring Janet Jackson, on Apple (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Justin Timberlake is set to release a four-part docuseries on Apple TV in December, described as a “tell-all,” three sources confirm to Variety. One source s...
articles.body:
Justin Timberlake is set to release a four-part docuseries on Apple TV in December, described as a "tell-all," three sources confirm to Variety.

One source says the series will feature Janet Jackson discussing the infamous "wardrobe malfunction" that took place during the pair's performance at the 2004 Super Bowl. Another source says that Timberlake discusses some of former girlfriend Britney Spears' recent comments as well.

Further details on the series, which is directed by Fisher Stevens, were not available at the time of this article's publication; reps for Timberlake, Jackson and Apple had no comment or did not respond to Variety 's multiple requests for comment.

Timberlake has a relationship with the streamer dating back to 2021, when he starred in the Apple Original film "Palmer."

The news comes during a comparatively low-profile period for Timberlake, who made a guest appearance during Jay-Z's concert in Paris last month but otherwise has been off the radar since his "Forget Tomorrow" global tour in support of his most recent album, "Everything I Thought It Was," which was released in March of 2024.

The singer announced in July 2025 that he has been diagnosed with Lyme disease, which affected some of his performances on the tour. Fans noticed that Timberlake appeared sluggish and low-energy during performances on the international leg of the trek, which he suggested was due to the nerve damage and fatigue he experienced from Lyme disease.

"I've been battling some health issues, and was diagnosed with Lyme Disease–which I don't say so you feel bad for me – but to shed some light on what I've been up against behind the scenes," he wrote. "If you've experienced this disease or know someone who has- then you're aware: Living with this can be relentlessly debilitating, both mentally and physically."

The tour, which wrapped in July of 2025, was further complicated by Timberlake's DWI conviction, stemming from his arrest in Sag Harbor, New York, the previous year. He was pulled over by police in June 2024 after running a stop sign and veering out of his lane. The incident took place shortly before the tour's launch, and Page Six reported that Timberlake said to officers, in a much-memed comment, "This is going to ruin the tour" — however, police bodycam footage released later showed that he did not say those words, rather something like "I'm on tour."
